summary: This work presents CLIQUE, a facility coupling an 18.5 MeV electron linear accelerator to a dilution refrigerator to study on-demand ionizing radiation effects in superconducting qubits, and demonstrates radiation-induced relaxation, excitation, detuning, and dephasing errors in a nine-qubit transmon chip with energy deposition closely matching cosmic-ray muons. Single linac electrons enable precise timing and rapid event statistics collection, revealing junction-orientation-dependent error signatures with low-gap-island qubits showing relaxation decay times of 6–9 ms versus 300–400 μs for high-gap-island qubits.
motivation: Ionizing radiation from cosmic-ray muons creates correlated errors across multiple qubits and threatens quantum error correction surface codes, but previous studies relied on stochastic ambient radiation sources or alternative quasiparticle generation methods that lack timing resolution or may not faithfully reproduce actual radiation effects.
method: A pulsed 18.5 MeV electron beam from a medical linear accelerator was directed at a multi-qubit transmon chip inside a dilution refrigerator, with sub-10 μs timing synchronization to the quantum control system and a scintillation detector for fluence monitoring; qubit states were measured following preparation with varying detection delays to capture relaxation, excitation, detuning, and dephasing errors.
result: Relaxation error amplitudes $A_{rel}$ ranged from 272–611 kHz with decay times $\tau_{rel}$ of 6.2–9.1 ms for low-gap-island qubits versus 370–414 kHz and 283–414 μs for high-gap-island qubits; detuning errors persisted 2–3× longer than relaxation errors, and a two-level rate model with exponentially decaying $\Gamma_{rel}$ and $\Gamma_{exc}$ successfully captured the competing error dynamics across all qubits and detection delays from 200 ns to 12 μs.
